one_month_reasoning: Q3 results are not expected inside the window: last year's Q3 came out Nov 10 and Q2 2026 on Aug 5, so expect early-to-mid November. Things that could land by Oct 31: (1) finalization of the investment-grade credit support on the Anthropic lease, which press reports tie to Anthropic's hardware-vendor choice 'within about four months' of early July, so roughly early November [13]; (2) launch or pricing of the reported ~$3.5B Justified debt package [12]; (3) commencement notices for the first CB-4 data halls (guided for 2H26) [1]. Each of these is a modest positive if it happens, but none is firmly dated. The stock fell 13% in the last week of September on insider-selling headlines and has drawn down 50% from its June high, so momentum and reversal pull in opposite directions. I stay close to neutral: median ~$14.85, monthly vol ~26% (91%/3.5), with a very slight downward tilt for continued supply from insider 10b5-1/144 sales.

bear.story: Anthropic IG credit wrap slips or comes on worse terms, the Justified $3.5B financing prices wide or needs more equity, CB-4/CB-5 deliveries slip, and AI-infrastructure multiples compress. The market moves toward a 10% WACC DCF ($6-8) and the Abernathy-style private mark.

base.story: CB-4/CB-5 delivered by 1H27 (438 MW live, ~$700M NOI run-rate), Justified financed and on track for 2H27 first delivery, at most one modest new lease. Stock trades between my DCF and the 8% cap-rate NAV.

bull.story: A 250-500 MW lease at Muskie or Lake Mariner signs with an IG hyperscaler, the Anthropic credit support finalizes, and data-center developers rerate toward 6-7% cap rates. That gets back toward the June highs and the $30-36 sell-side targets.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$7.50 the equity (about $4.6B diluted) would be worth less than a 10% WACC DCF of the contracted leases with no pipeline value. That would most likely mean a fundamental break: the Anthropic credit support or Justified financing failed, a tenant problem at Fluidstack, a large cost overrun at CB-4/CB-5, or a dilutive rescue raise. Ordinary 91%-vol noise alone should not take it there.

reasoning: Sources are mostly primary: 10-Q, 8-Ks, the Q2 deck and the call. The contracted book is ~839 MW: Lake Mariner 438 MW (~$8.5B over 10 yrs, Google-backstopped Fluidstack plus Core42) and Justified 401 MW with Anthropic ($19B over 20 yrs, delivered 2H27-1H28). At 85% margins that is ~$1.5B of stabilized NOI. About $6.3B of capex is still to come ($1.7B+$0.15B at LM, ~$4.4B at Justified), against $5.7B of debt, $3.0B of cash and $0.53B of Abernathy proceeds, on ~615M diluted shares. At $14.91 the market cap is ~$9.2B and the EV ~$11.5B, before the remaining capex. My DCF at a 9% WACC, with the 10-yr Treasury at 5.24%, gives ~$10.4 today and ~$11.6 in 12 months. A NAV at an 8% cap rate gives ~$15.5. The only observed private-market mark is TeraWulf's own Abernathy sale at ~7.3x NOI, which implies far less (~$3.9). The blended fair value is ~$11.8, about 20% below spot, and sell-side targets ($30-36 in July) sit far above me. Insiders were mostly net sellers in Aug-Sep, though a director bought at $14.79. Over 12 months, sentiment and 91% vol matter more than fair value. So I built the ladder from a scenario mixture (bear $7.5/30%, base $13.5/45%, bull $26/25%) blended with a lognormal (median $13.5, sigma ~0.85). That gives a median a bit below spot, P(>= $14.91) ~0.46, and fat tails both ways. Limits: no consensus estimates (Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and Twelve Data targets need a paid plan), and the DCD article was blocked.
